name: Saint Basil`s Cathedral (Color)
description: Basil's Cathedral, located at the southern end of the Red Square outside the Moscow Kremlin, is an Orthodox cathedral built by Russian architects Barma and Postnik under the orders of Tsar Ivan the Great. It was completed in 1560. The nine colorful onion-shaped church roofs are his characteristic symbol, and the overall design reflects the Russian folk architectural art style of the 16th century. Pinku has highly restored the nine iconic church roofs, hollowed-out windows and textures, reproducing the historical imprint behind the churches in details.
